claim.pdf_says: 14.9.22.3   Syntax rules — a fourth-level clause heading, set in the same style and at the same level as 14.9.22.1 General and 14.9.22.2 General formats on page 673.
claim.why_it_matters: Its siblings are transcribed as `### 14.9.22.1 General` and `### 14.9.22.2 General formats`, and every neighbouring statement uses `###` for its `.3 Syntax rules` clause (`### 14.9.25.3`, `### 14.9.26.3`, `### 14.9.27.3`, `### 14.9.29.3`). Emitting 14.9.22.3 at `##` promotes it to sibling-of-the-statement rank, so any tool that builds a section tree from heading depth files the INSPECT syntax rules outside the INSPECT statement. `## 14.9.22.4 General rules` (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 27892) has the identical defect.

verdict.reasoning: REFUTED on five independent grounds; nothing is missing and nothing changes meaning. (1) The heading is NOT missing, so the claim's own kind is factually wrong. The PDF page 674 (printed folio 644) prints '14.9.22.3 Syntax rules' immediately below the 'where replacement-item is:' figure. specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 27853 (page-674 workunit line 47) reads '## 14.9.22.3 Syntax rules'. The clause number and the title are transcribed verbatim and correctly. The entire alleged discrepancy is the count of '#' characters in a Markdown heading marker. (2) The PDF has no Markdown heading levels to lose, and gives no typographic level cue. I rendered page 673 at 300 dpi and compared the glyphs directly: '14.9.22 INSPECT statement', '14.9.22.1 General' and '14.9.22.2 General formats' are all set in the SAME bold serif face at the SAME size. ISO conveys clause depth exclusively through the dotted clause NUMBER, not through type size or weight. The markdown reproduces that number exactly ('14.9.22.3'), so the depth information the PDF actually carries is fully preserved. There is no PDF property that '##' contradicts. (3) The transcription carries an explicit, correct structural signal on the line directly above: `` (line 27852), matching `` at line 27891. Any consumer building a section tree has an unambiguous machine-readable hierarchy keyed to the clause number itself. (4) The stated harm is impossible as described, because heading depth is already not a section-tree signal in this document. specs/ISO_COBOL.md contains 941 running-header headings '# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)' and 1261 page markers '## Page NNN' interleaved throughout the body. A tool that 'builds a section tree from heading depth' is already broken by ~2200 pieces of page furniture sitting at the `#` and `##` levels — including one `## Page 674` eleven lines above the disputed heading. 14.9.22.3 could not be the thing that misfiles the INSPECT syntax rules. (5) The claim misquotes the corpus and misframes a document-wide convention as a page-674 defect. 'Every neighbouring statement uses ### for its .3 Syntax rules clause' is false: `## 14.9.28.3 Syntax rules` (PERFORM, line 29150) is also `##`. For the `.4 General rules` clause the claim's preferred level is the MINORITY across the same neighbourhood — `##` at 14.9.20.4, 14.9.22.4, 14.9.23.4, 14.9.24.4, 14.9.25.4, 14.9.26.4, 14.9.27.4 and 14.9.28.4, versus `###` at only 14.9.21.4 and 14.9.29.4. Measured across the whole file, four-part clause numbers appear as `##` 162 times, `###` 620 times and `####` 24 times; three-part clause numbers appear as `##` 276 times, `###` 508 times and `####` 17 times. Heading depth is uncorrelated with clause depth throughout all 1261 pages. 14.9.22.3 and 14.9.22.4 are ordinary members of a 162-instance population, not a localized transcription error against the PDF. This falls squarely within the stated rejection criteria: the 'missing' text is present, the difference is only formatting, and the meaning is unchanged. No COBOL semantics are affected — the INSPECT syntax rules text on page 674 (rules 1 and 2 under ALL FORMATS) is transcribed completely and accurately, and no conformance behavior derives from a Markdown heading level.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a PDF-vs-markdown discrepancy. The heading '14.9.22.3 Syntax rules' is present, correctly numbered and correctly titled at specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 27853, with a correct `` anchor above it. The only difference is the Markdown heading marker depth (`##` rather than `###`), which corresponds to nothing in the PDF: page 673 shows ISO sets 14.9.22, 14.9.22.1 and 14.9.22.2 in identical bold type and signals depth solely via the dotted clause number, which the transcription preserves verbatim. If anyone wants uniform heading depth it is a cosmetic, whole-file normalization task — 162 four-part and 276 three-part clause numbers sit at `##` across the document, and the file additionally carries 941 `#` running headers and 1261 `## Page NNN` markers that would have to be de-leveled first — not a page-674 spec-reconciliation finding.
